why: Count the small squares in each figure. Figures 1, 3, 4 and 5 are each made of exactly 5 small squares, joined corner to corner or edge to edge. Figure 2 is made of 6 small squares. So figure 2 is the odd one out. Figure 1 looks very different from figure 5, but both still have 5 squares, so the shape does not matter, only the count.
trick: When all the figures are built from small repeated parts, count the parts first before you look at the layout.
note: Rule is the number of small squares (5 in four figures, 6 in figure 2).
